newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares down on speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares down on speculative selling.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed lower on Tuesday due to speculative selling, with most institutions remaining sidelined and market-moving news absent, brokers said.
The B share index edged down 0.82 points, or 0.91 percent, to end at 89.85 on turnover of HK$12.95 million, compared with HK$13.57 million in the previous session.

Shenbao was the sharpest loser on speculative selling, brokers said. The counter fell HK$0.20, or 8.51 percent, to HK$2.15 on thin trade of 35,100 shares. Tellus Machinery followed suit, slumping HK$0.14, or 7.69 percent, to HK$1.68.
Dadonghai, the most active counter, slipped HK$0.01 to HK$1.31 on trade volume of 1.11 million shares on profit-taking, brokers said.
Fangda, which gained sharply on Monday, fell back HK$0.01 to HK$4.48 after 449,600 shares changed hands.
Floppy disk maker Benelux reversed early heavy losses and ended up HK$0.10, or 3.64 percnnt, at HK$2.85, with only 31,000 shares traded.

Jiangling Motors gained HK$0.05, or 2.60 percent, to HK$1.97 on the session's third most active trade of 316,600 shares. Brokers said the issue's rise was linked to the imminent listing of its counterpart Chongqing Changan Automobile Co Ltd scheduled for Friday.

The A share market lost ground on Tuesday on selling triggered by rumours that Beijing intended to change the existing stock trading settlement system from next-day to a three-day wait as part of its counter-speculation measures.
An official at the Shenzhen bourse contacted by telephone said the exchange had not received any instructions from Beijing on the subject and declined to comment further.

The A share index sank 3.01 points, or 0.77 percent, to end at 385.72, with turnover expanding to 9.59 billion yuan from 8.27 billion yuan on Monday. The composite index lost 2.82 points, or 0.78 percent, to 358.97.
The pharmaceutical issue Hainan Haiyao was the target of profit-taking, brokers said. The issue tumbled 0.94 yuan, or 6.49 percent, to 13.55 yuan.

Computer components maker Beijing Bit Co Ltd, which listed 20 million A shares and 3.20 million staff shares in Shenzhen on Tuesday, ended the session at 14.98 yuan as volume hit 17.93 million shares.
The A shares were issued at 4.76 yuan per share via the Shenzhen bourse's automated quotation system last month, while the staff shares were offered at one yuan per share in 1993.
